title: Five Ways to Point
label: ch:fr-pointing
canDo: I can say that something exists, say what it is, hand somebody over, point at a noun, and answer the question where.

payoff.summary: Everything the book owns is pointed at five ways: it exists, it is a thing, it is handed over, it is pointed at in front of its noun, and it is somewhere. One Latin word runs under four of the five -- ecce, 'behold', which fused into ce, ici, voici and voila and then vanished inside all of them.
payoff.note: The cheapest chapter in the French inventory: five items close five points, because four of them are single-phrase constructions the track had never named and the fifth rides on the article system the opening chapter already taught.
